section_summary: This section records reactions to the Strike Report and proposals to raise Japan’s industrial capacity while limiting reparations. It includes press coverage from New Zealand and China, State and Army discussions of occupation policy, and British concerns about changes to United States policy. The final pages introduce Japanese industry’s financial, labor, and management problems.

subfiles.title: Reaction to the Strike Report on Japanese Reparations
subfiles.from: John S. Service, American Legation, Wellington
subfiles.about: Reports limited New Zealand reaction to the Strike Report.
subfiles.summary: Service notes one news article and no government or major editorial response. He quotes a hostile Standard column questioning Japan’s demilitarization and American occupation policy.

subfiles.title: Rebuild Japanese Industry: U.S. Report Opposes Present Policy
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Strike Report’s recommendations and anticipated conflict over reparations.
subfiles.summary: The article describes proposals to retain Japanese heavy industry and predicts disagreement between the Army, State Department, and reparations claimants.

subfiles.title: Civil Property Custodian Problems in Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends coordinated guidance to MacArthur on civil property custody.
subfiles.summary: Dupuy proposes an Army message grounded in State–Army coordination instead of further formal directives.

subfiles.title: Civil Property Custodian Problems in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to Draper on SCAP authority and civil property custody.
subfiles.summary: Claxton distinguishes the general question of SCAP authority from particular custody issues and asks Martin to consult Allison and Snow.

subfiles.title: Civil Property Custodian Problems
subfiles.about: Proposes interpreting existing directives broadly to resolve property custody questions.
subfiles.summary: Dupuy reports Tansey’s urgent need for guidance on United Nations property, German and other foreign assets, and Japanese patents. He recommends that SCAP seek Washington’s guidance under existing directives, avoiding delays in the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Draft Message to MacArthur on Civil Property Custodian Matters
subfiles.about: Proposes withdrawing property papers and clarifying SCAP’s existing authority.
subfiles.summary: The draft seeks MacArthur’s views on handling several asset and patent questions.

subfiles.title: Local Reaction to the Strike Report
subfiles.about: Reports two Shanghai editorials critical of American plans for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cabot summarizes Chinese fears of Japanese rearmament and revived industry, including concern over Hoffman’s appointment to administer aid.

subfiles.title: Chinese Press Review: Prevent Japan from Rearming and Japan Is Rising
subfiles.about: Translates and extracts Chinese editorials on Japan’s recovery and regional security.
subfiles.summary: The review includes the Sin Wen Pao and Yi Shih Pao editorials cited in Cabot’s despatch, along with other press items. Its principal articles warn that industrial recovery, merchant shipping, and looser occupation controls could restore Japanese military strength. They urge Chinese safeguards and stronger Chinese productive capacity.

subfiles.title: Local Reaction to Strike Report
subfiles.about: Reports editorials demanding Japanese reparations and criticizing United States policy.
subfiles.summary: Cabot describes one editorial insisting on China’s reparations entitlement and another warning against unilateral American changes to Japan policy.

subfiles.title: Chinese Press Review: We Insist Upon Receiving Japanese Reparations
subfiles.about: Summarizes Chinese editorials opposing reduced reparations and changed occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: The Chung Yang Jih Pao editorial invokes the Potsdam Declaration against Draper’s position on industrial removals. Other press excerpts address unrelated Chinese affairs; the concluding Tung Nan Jih Pao item criticizes unilateral American measures toward Japan.

subfiles.title: Chinese Press Review No. 616
subfiles.about: Reviews Chinese commentary on the Foreign Assistance Act and use of American aid.
subfiles.summary: Editorial extracts discuss aid’s economic benefits, Cold War implications, and distribution in China.

subfiles.title: Forthcoming Strike Report
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman and Philander P. Claxton Jr.
subfiles.about: Warns that the forthcoming report will propose higher Japanese industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: Wisner relays Draper’s expectation that Royall may publish the report.

subfiles.title: Recommendations on Draper Correspondence and Industrial Retention Conferences
subfiles.about: Recommends preparing Lovett for review of Japanese reparations policy.
subfiles.summary: Claxton reviews a proposed reply to Draper and Thorp’s principles for retention and reparations. He recommends briefing Lovett with policy history and comparative figures, then convening officials to discuss the imminent Strike Report.

subfiles.title: Review of Japanese Reparations Program with Mr. Lovett
subfiles.about: Suggests a policy meeting with Lovett before the consultants report arrives.
subfiles.summary: Martin recommends including Thorp and Butterworth in the discussion.

subfiles.title: Forthcoming Strike Report
subfiles.about: Argues against publishing the unapproved Strike Report.
subfiles.summary: Whitman argues that publication would expose classified policy material, confuse public debate, and complicate Far Eastern Commission negotiations. He also cautions that the consultants may address occupation matters outside their assigned expertise.

subfiles.title: Publicity on Strike Report
subfiles.about: Raises the risk of an unauthorized release by Strike.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum urges coordination with Draper; annotations record Army consultation and a request for a State position.

subfiles.title: Request for Overseas Consultants Report
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests a copy of the consultants’ report on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Friedrich requests the report for a study of wartime industrial change.

subfiles.title: Reply to Professor Friedrich
subfiles.about: Directs the report request to the Department of the Army.
subfiles.summary: Whitman explains that the report was prepared for the Army.

subfiles.title: Deconcentration Review Board
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s announcement of the Deconcentration Review Board.
subfiles.summary: Royall welcomes the board’s broad authority and MacArthur’s stated concern for economic recovery.

subfiles.title: MacArthur’s Announcement of the Deconcentration Review Board
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for Secretary Royall
subfiles.about: Announces the board’s membership, mandate, and approach to company reorganization.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur identifies five board members and gives the board broad authority to review deconcentration standards and company plans. The message says companies will be removed from consideration where reorganization is unnecessary or harmful to production. Confidential passages describe the progress of reviews and MacArthur’s intention to avoid disruption of Japan’s economy.

subfiles.title: Japanese Reparations and Level of Industry
subfiles.about: Records British concerns about unilateral American changes to Japan policy.
subfiles.summary: Ford warns that sharply higher Japanese industrial levels could undo Far Eastern Commission agreement, provoke British criticism, and push members toward opposition to the United States. He favors using existing agreed policy flexibly and stresses Japan’s need for self-support without alienating its neighbors.

subfiles.title: Local Comment on the Strike Report
subfiles.about: Relays a Chinese editorial on conditions for Japan’s economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: The damaged OCR indicates concern that recovery must be accompanied by safeguards against renewed monopoly and militarism.

subfiles.title: Watch the Japanese Industrial-Commercial Mission Closely
subfiles.about: Reports a Shanghai editorial warning about a Japanese commercial mission.
subfiles.summary: The editorial links a planned mission involving former Mitsui and Mitsubishi personnel to revived Japanese ambitions and calls for an early peace treaty.

subfiles.title: J. & P. Coats Factory in Japan
subfiles.about: Suggests discussions about restarting the Coats factory in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Percival proposes provisional talks on cotton yarn supplies and working capital pending policy decisions.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement for Wellington Despatch 138
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy of the despatch.
subfiles.summary: The sheet instructs staff to return the replacement copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Articles on Revival of Japanese Industry
subfiles.about: Forwards New Zealand Truth articles criticizing Japanese industrial revival.
subfiles.summary: The Legation submits articles as evidence of public comment on Japan policy.

subfiles.title: Deepening Harm of Japan: Britain’s Interest
subfiles.about: Criticizes Britain’s response to American plans for Japanese industrial recovery.
subfiles.summary: The article argues that revived Japanese production could threaten Dominion trade and Pacific security. It urges Britain to heed Australian and New Zealand concerns about American policy.

subfiles.title: Concern Over U.S. Plans
subfiles.about: Reports Australian pressure on Britain over United States plans for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The article describes British cabinet divisions and Australian fears of renewed Japanese power.

subfiles.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries on Financial, Labor, and Industrial Problems
subfiles.about: Transmits five memoranda by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries president Yasujiro Okano.
subfiles.summary: Johnson outlines Okano’s views on labor relations, finance, management purges, and legislation.
